messages.author: 20d266bb5c67a8cc
messages.subject: bug in stat_spoke()
parts:
Hi everyone,

I tried to use stat_spoke(), similar to the example from the ggplot
homepage, I paste the example here again
(http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/stat_spoke.html):

df <- expand.grid(x = 1:10, y=1:10)
df$angle <- runif(100, 0, 2*pi)
df$speed <- runif(100, 0, 0.5)
qplot(x, y, data=df) + stat_spoke(aes(angle=angle), radius = 0.5)

When I try to use that with a reverse y-axis, the output becomes messed
up. It looks like the basepoints of the spokes get transformed, but the
endpoints are calculated (from angle and radius) without transformation:


qplot(x, y, data=df) + stat_spoke(aes(angle=angle), radius =
0.5)+scale_y_reverse()

The same happens (of course) with ...+scale_y_continuous(trans="reverse").

Please advise me whether this is a bug or whether I am missing some
point here?

Thanks,
Martin
